subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Predicting the content of a talk (Listening 1.4.1)
outcomes: Predict which phrases relate to malls, markets or both
Listen to a tour guide's talk and sort phrases correctly

tf.s: The tour guide talks about shopping in malls and souqs in Muscat.
tf.why: Those are the two kinds of places in the talk.

tf.s: According to the guide, shopping malls are best for quick, easy shopping.
tf.why: Malls make shopping fast and easy.

tf.s: Opportunities for bargaining exist mainly in shopping malls.
Tourists love the narrow passages and tiny shops of the souqs.
tf.why: They enjoy the traditional market style.

tf.s: A multi-level car park is a typical feature of a traditional souq.
tf.why: It is a feature of a modern mall.

tf.s: Every phrase in the list is mentioned in the talk.
Two of the phrases apply to both malls and markets.
Predicting before listening helps you know what to listen for.
tf.why: Predictions prepare you for the talk.

tf.s: The phrases in the talk come in exactly the same order as the list.
tf.why: The order in the talk is different.

tf.s: The guide says the souqs have friendly shopkeepers.
tf.why: Friendly shopkeepers are part of the souq's charm.

boxes.q: Where is quick, easy shopping best?

boxes.why: Bargaining is part of souq shopping.
The speaker is a tour guide.

boxes.q: How many phrases are not in the talk?
How many phrases apply to both places?
Which is a feature of malls?
Which is a feature of souqs?
Which city is the talk about?
boxes.why: The guide talks about shopping in Muscat.

boxes.q: What should you do before listening?
What do you write while listening?
boxes.why: You note numbers of phrases you hear.

mcq.q: According to the guide, which place is best for quick, easy shopping?
Where do opportunities for bargaining exist?
mcq.why: Bargaining is part of the souq experience.

mcq.q: How many phrases in the list are not in the talk?
What do tourists love about souqs?
o: narrow passages, tiny shops and friendly shopkeepers
mcq.why: These give the souq its traditional style.

mcq.q: Which phrase would you put in the 'Malls' column?
mcq.why: Big car parks are typical of malls.

mcq.q: Which phrase would you put in the 'Markets' column?
A tourist wants a traditional shopping experience and likes to bargain. Where should she go?
Why is it useful to predict where phrases belong before listening?
o: You know what to listen for, so it is easier to follow
You do not need to listen
It gives you all the answers
mcq.why: Prediction prepares you for the content.

mcq.q: Why do some phrases go in both columns?
o: They describe features shared by malls and markets
They are not in the talk
mcq.why: Two phrases apply to both places.

mcq.q: Why might someone say both souqs and malls are a shopper's paradise?
o: Each offers variety in its own way
mcq.why: Malls and souqs each have their own good points.
